title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-02-27
source: Ampex MM-1000 16 Track Master Two Inch Wide Tape; Multi Track Mix-down To DAT By Dan Healy @ 44.1KHz) circa 1995?; DAT x ONE by Dick Latvala- DAT x TWO via either Dick or Rob Bertrando; Editing (Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name); Jim Wise; This is a 100% Flat transfer from the DAT no signal processing what-so-ever

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard‑derived recording that captures a legendary Fillmore West show highlighted by a quintessential Dark Star → St. Stephen stretch and crystal‑clear band interplay.
ai_review.review: The 16‑track SBD mix delivers remarkably clear, crisp audio – Tom’s keyboards and Bob’s rhythm guitar shine through, while Jerry’s tone moves from fuzzy to ear‑piercing during the epic Dark Star.  The performance itself is often cited as a benchmark for the era, with a tight first set and a second set that peaks on Dark Star → St. Stephen, Mountains of the Moon, and a fiery Cosmic Charlie finish.

ai_rating.rationale: All but one review are five‑star praises focusing on both superb musical moments and high‑fidelity sound; the lone zero‑star appears to be an outlier, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with excellent separation – Tom’s keys and Bob’s rhythm guitar are especially clear; Jerry’s guitar tone is vivid.  No significant drop‑outs or muffiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise first set that showcases tight playing (Good Morning… / Doin' That Rag), followed by a second‑set climax with the classic Dark Star → St. Stephen sequence, expansive jam on Mountains of the Moon, and a high‑energy finish with Cosmic Charlie.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar moves from fuzzy to ear‑piercing, delivering iconic “ta‑da‑Da” sequences during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work described as an impressive ‘maelstrom’, anchoring the improvisations.
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar is noted for its clarity and creative presence throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom’s keyboards are clearly audible and well‑balanced in the mix, a rarity on some releases.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally solid; one reviewer mentions louder drums in certain mixes but no major issues.
